industrial_fats.name: Palm Oil
industrial_fats.risk: High in saturated palmitic acid (approx. 50%), which elevates LDL ('bad') cholesterol and cardiovascular risk when consumed chronically. Used primarily for low wholesale cost and long shelf stability.

industrial_fats.name: Palmolein
industrial_fats.risk: The liquid fraction obtained by fractionating palm oil. Ubiquitous in Indian packaged namkeens, chips, and instant noodles due to low cost and high thermal stability for repeated frying.

industrial_fats.name: Palm Kernel Oil
industrial_fats.risk: Extracted from the kernel of the palm fruit; exceptionally high in saturated fat (over 80%), similar to coconut oil, but heavily refined and stripped of natural micronutrients.

industrial_fats.name: Hydrogenated Vegetable Oil
industrial_fats.risk: Industrial catalytic hydrogenation turns liquid vegetable oils into solid fats. Partial hydrogenation generates artificial trans-fatty acids, proven to raise LDL, lower HDL, and cause vascular endothelial inflammation.

industrial_fats.name: Vanaspati
industrial_fats.risk: Historically high in trans fats (capped at 2% by FSSAI in 2022). High in saturated fatty acids and associated with cardiovascular disease.

industrial_fats.name: Interesterified Vegetable Fat
industrial_fats.risk: Engineered replacement for trans-fats created by chemically rearranging fatty acids on the glycerol backbone. Clinical trials show adverse impacts on glucose metabolism and post-prandial lipemia.

industrial_fats.name: Fractionated Palm Oil
industrial_fats.risk: Hard solid fraction of palm oil utilized as a cheap cocoa butter substitute (CBR/CBS) in confectioneries and biscuit fillings.

industrial_fats.name: Refined Cottonseed Oil
industrial_fats.risk: High in inflammatory Omega-6 linoleic acid (over 50%); requires intensive caustic refining, bleaching, and deodorizing to remove natural gossypol.
